scope: Name FUN_00576CD0 (top remaining s2c gap: 1621 pcap hits, opcode 0x0190, per the pcap opcode coverage matrix pass). Cross-reference bahamut_opcodes.json to identify the wire opcode name, decomp the handler + its 3-tier worker chain, characterize the cluster siblings 0x018F + 0x0191. Catalog the uncataloged worker / data-writer / cleanup functions.

method.step1: Cross-reference bahamut_opcodes.json: opcode 400 (0x0190) = MapServerOpcode::MassSetItemModifier. Siblings: 0x018F = MassSetItemModifierBegin, 0x0191 = MassSetItemModifierEnd. Three-phase streaming protocol for mass item modifier updates.
method.step2: Bulk-decomp FUN_00576CD0 plus cluster (FUN_0076BE60 worker, FUN_00768C40 writer, FUN_00766920 cleanup, FUN_00576C60 + FUN_0076BE30 = 0x18F sibling, FUN_00576D40 + FUN_0076BF10 = 0x191 sibling). 8 functions via DumpFunctionDecomp.java.
method.step3: Identify the 109-byte dispatcher shape (SEH + critical section enter/leave + manager+worker call) shared across all three dispatchers FUN_00576C60/00576CD0/00576D40. FUN_00cc9320 = CS enter, FUN_00cc9330 = CS leave; the manager pointer is *param_1 (the dispatcher arg, a zone-local manager object).
method.step4: Characterize FUN_00768C40 as the record writer: copies 8-byte header (packet[0..1]) to target+0x8/+0xC + zeroes target+0x14/+0x18/+0x1C + allocates 64 bytes via FUN_00783ec0(0x40,0) + copies 16 dwords (64 bytes) from packet[2..18] into *(target+0x14). Total wire body read = 8 + 64 = 72 bytes; the unmapped payload decoding pass's body_length=120 implies remaining 48 bytes are reserved/unread tail.
method.step5: Characterize FUN_00766920 as the record cleanup: conditionally allocates new (FUN_0089B8D0 / FUN_0089BCA0) and conditionally frees old (FUN_00765A90 + _free).
method.step6: Confirm existing catalog entries at 0x00576CD0: BCS-Y-0574 'S2cDispatcher_HighSwitch_Case190_FUN_00576CD0' (correct opcode) and BCS-Y-0598 'EquipmentDispatcher_Opcode0x018F_FUN_00576CD0' (MISLABELED - opcode in name should be 0x0190 not 0x018F). The equipment subsystem pass's manifest swapped the 0x018F / 0x0190 case-table mappings (its 'high_branch_mass_modifier' table is inverted). Fix the BCS-Y-0598 name via Edit.

key_findings: Opcode 0x0190 is MapServerOpcode::MassSetItemModifier - a per-record body packet in a 3-phase streaming protocol (Begin 0x018F -> Body 0x0190 emitted N times -> End 0x0191). The 1621 pcap hits represent many bodies across all captures - the per-modifier-record rate is what makes this the 2nd-heaviest s2c opcode.

Wire format: 8-byte header (target id + sub-id; written to manager+0x8 and +0xC) + 64-byte modifier-data block (16 dwords; written to a freshly-allocated 64-byte buffer stored at manager+0x14). Total body read = 72 bytes; the unmapped payload decoding pass observed body_length=120 means 48 bytes of payload tail are unread by the cataloged handler path (reserved or used by a sibling path).

The 3 dispatchers FUN_00576C60 / 00576CD0 / 00576D40 share an identical 109-byte shape: critical section enter (FUN_00cc9320 on *param_1) -> worker call -> critical section leave (FUN_00cc9330). The locked object is the zone-local MassSetItemModifier manager pointed to by *param_1.

The 3 workers FUN_0076BE30 / 0076BE60 / 0076BF10 are sized 34 / 168 / 149 bytes - Begin is minimal (3 calls, no data write), Body does the real write via FUN_00768C40 (173-byte record writer that allocates 64 bytes and copies 16 dwords), End does 6-call finalize (notifies subscribers, releases the manager).
Shared helper FUN_0076B950 is called by all 3 workers - probably the manager state-machine validator or transaction step counter. Not separately cataloged (call site is shared infrastructure).

The equipment subsystem pass's high_branch_mass_modifier table SWAPPED 0x018F and 0x0190 - it says 0x018F = FUN_00576CD0 (wrong; that's 0x190) and 0x0190 = FUN_00576C60 (wrong; that's 0x18F). The high switch enumeration pass is correct (its case-label decimal vs hex disambiguation note confirms Ghidra's printing convention: case 400 = 0x190 = FUN_00576CD0). BCS-Y-0598 inherits this swap bug in its name - fixed via Edit in this manifest.

MassSetItemModifier is NOT equipment-specific per se (the equipment subsystem pass framed it that way because the equipment subsystem touches item modifiers). 'Item modifier' in 1.x is a broader concept covering inventory item state mutations - equipment stat changes, item charge counts, durability, etc. The mass variant streams bulk modifications efficiently during bulk operations (e.g., a full equipment swap, or a vendor restock that updates many items).

proposed_bcs_y_entries.name: MassSetItemModifier_Op0190_Worker_FUN_0076BE60
proposed_bcs_y_entries.summary: 168-byte worker for s2c 0x0190 MassSetItemModifier. Called from MassSetItemModifier_Op0190_Dispatcher_FUN_00576CD0 inside the critical section. Calls FUN_0076b950 (shared manager helper), FUN_009d1b35 (guard check), and on success FUN_00768c40 (the record writer). Always calls FUN_00766920 cleanup afterward.

proposed_bcs_y_entries.name: MassSetItemModifier_RecordWriter_FUN_00768C40
proposed_bcs_y_entries.summary: 173-byte record writer for s2c 0x0190 MassSetItemModifier per-record body. Writes 8-byte header (packet[0..1] = target_id + sub_id) to target+0x8/+0xC, zeroes target+0x14/+0x18/+0x1C, allocates a 64-byte buffer via FUN_00783ec0(0x40, 0), then memcpy-loops 16 dwords (64 bytes) from packet+8 into *(target+0x14). Total wire body read = 72 bytes.

proposed_bcs_y_entries.name: MassSetItemModifier_RecordCleanup_FUN_00766920
proposed_bcs_y_entries.summary: 207-byte cleanup function for s2c 0x0190 record processing. Conditionally allocates a fresh record via FUN_0089B8D0 / FUN_0089BCA0 (if guard FUN_009d1b35 reports new), and conditionally frees the prior record via FUN_00765A90 + _free (if param_1 is non-null). Effectively rotates the manager's active-record slot.

proposed_bcs_y_entries.name: MassSetItemModifier_ProtocolSynthesis
proposed_bcs_y_entries.summary: Three-phase MassSetItemModifier streaming protocol synthesis. Server bulk-updates item modifiers (equipment stats / inventory state / item charges) via opcodes 0x018F (Begin), 0x0190 (Body, N records, each carrying 8B header + 64B modifier-data block, 72 wire bytes of 120 read), 0x0191 (End). All three dispatchers share the FUN_00576C60-style 109-byte SEH-wrapped + critical-section-locked shape; all three workers share FUN_0076b950 manager helper. The body opcode 0x0190 is the 2nd-heaviest s2c opcode in pcap (1621 hits; the pcap opcode coverage matrix pass's topUncoveredS2cGaps rank 1). Closes that gap. (Note entry uses opcode 0x0190 dispatcher VA for indexing; deduplicates against the existing dispatcher entry by address-skip - this synthesis intentionally not added as a separate symbol.)
